key_insight: Quantum-kernel classification can distinguish quantum states with polynomially many measurements when sufficient conditions on the data structure hold.
engineering_relevance: A programmable photonic processor demonstrates a route to classifying Gaussian and non-Gaussian quantum states on currently available quantum hardware.
method: Derive sufficient data-structure conditions for accurate classification with polynomial measurement cost.
Apply the framework to stellar rank, a measure of continuous-variable non-Gaussianity.
Prepare and process photonic states and perform virtual projections for kernel-based classification.
evidence_signal: The experiment accurately classified single-mode continuous-variable states of stellar rank zero and one despite experimental imperfections.
watch_item: The experimental demonstration covers only single-mode states of stellar rank zero and one; broader scaling and applicability require further validation.
paper_title: Provably efficient experimental classification of quantum data with quantum kernels
